text:
[NDBG.4.3] `ds_engine_refracted_activations(engine, rule_filter, cb, user)` lists
every activation refraction blocks: each entry of the terminals' refraction
sets ([IRET.11.3]), with the rule name, the reason (`"refraction"` in v1), the
matched fact ids and a detail. An entry stays listed until its activation is
re-created ([IRET.11.3.2]); an unrelated assert or retract, or a pump boundary,
removes nothing. Every fact an entry names is therefore live. Use it to explain
"this rule matched but did not re-fire."

The runtime **must** report the entries in this order: terminals by ordinal
([LDET.5.4]), and within one terminal by their matched fact ids, compared as a
tuple, element by element, ascending. The matched fact ids are the facts the
author's patterns bound, in pattern order; a fact the compiler synthesised (the
clock tick, an `after` timer) is not one of them, so an entry whose match holds
only synthesised facts lists none. The detail is the text
`fired, and not re-created since`.
